ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the base BC of triangle ABC is horizontal, with B on the left, C on the right, and A above. Point D is located on side AC, and segment BD passes through the interior point E. Point F is located on the base BC, and A, E, F are collinear. Reasoning: According to the affine coordinate method, let B=(0,0), C=(1,0), A=(u,h). Then the area of triangle ABC is proportional to height h, specifically [ABC]=h/2. Because AD:DC=1:2, D is one third of the way from A to C, D=(2/3)A+(1/3)C. Because E is the midpoint of BD, and B is the origin, E=D/2=(1/3)A+(1/6)C. Therefore the y-coordinate of E is h/3. The line AE intersects the base BC at y=0 at F. Substituting A=(u,h), E=(u/3+1/6,h/3) into the parametric equation of the line gives the intersection point F=(1/4,0), so BF/BC=1/4. The area ratio of triangle EBF to triangle ABC equals the base ratio times the height ratio, namely (BF/BC)*(height from E to BC / height from A to BC)=(1/4)*(1/3)=1/12. Therefore [EBF]=360*(1/12)=30.

Since D is one-third of the way from A to C, D=(2/3)A+(1/3)C. Since E is the midpoint of BD and B is the origin, E=D/2=(1/3)A+(1/6)C. Parametrize line AE and intersect it with y=0 to get F=(1/4)C, so BF/BC=1/4. The height of E above BC is h/3.
